mathematicalInterpretation.mainFinding: For this one repeated-prefix discovery contrast, the own baseline changes the finite normalized response substantially despite a relatively accurate raw H1 difference. Both the gain of the gamma-weighted displacement term and the baseline-aligned denominator term matter. A positive signed cross reinforces their mismatch; this is not a large angular error in D, nor a pure radius-only endpoint repair.
mathematicalInterpretation.denominator: All response and component relative norms below use ||Z(b)-Z(a)||, unless explicitly labelled nativeD or native endpoint. Norm ratios are not causal shares. The full512 comparison summaries include511 unchanged rows per branch and must not replace the row9 response denominator.

crossings.interpretation: The predicted admitted displacement on the native base remains close in response; a native admitted displacement on the own base does not. Both ordered paths retain negative cross terms. They support baseline dependence, not a unique radius-versus-direction causal allocation.

errorComponents.interpretation: D and B errors reinforce in the complete error account. R is smaller here but retained; it includes finite source-policy discrepancy and rounding of the FP64 explanatory evaluation. Tiny G/g are regrouping records, not absent-by-definition.

radii.interpretation: Native radius shrinks while own radius grows. This reverses the sign of the inverse-radius change. B additionally contains the baseline vector and gamma, so it is not a scalar-only causal term.

endpoints.interpretation: These use their corresponding native finiteZ endpoint norms. They preserve the large baseline geometry error; high response cosine alone does not establish a usable state.

finiteClosure.interpretation: Final vector closure is observed zero at this evaluated precision. Nonzero intermediate g/G and the signed scalar Gram residual remain evidence; zero final closure does not assert exact real-arithmetic decomposition or unavailable107 intermediate parity.

mathematicalInterpretation.explanatoryLaw: For actual admitted endpoints h,k, D=Gamma*(k-h)/s(k), B=Gamma*h*(1/s(k)-1/s(h)), R=rho(k)-rho(h), with source-policy Z and separately retained ordered-sum g. Contrasts subtract actual edge components and preserve a further regrouping term and final closure.
causalLimits: Six source-policy normalization reconstructions are new original arithmetic; normalized intermediates were unavailable107, so this is not directly measured parity to those missing fields.
Row9 is one already-inspected causal prefix, repeated in vessel pairs rather than an independent replication. Neither1022 controls nor six states create a broad sample.
Pre-affine error norms cannot uniquely explain the historical Q/K/V errors: projection directions and denominators differ. No new projection was performed.
The separate fixed-nine-atom vessel-padding capacity shortfall remains. Neither normalization analysis nor a good row9 correction would produce missing history-dependent responses.

scalarDirectionInference.authority: Three published evaluated FP64 energies; inferred polarization, not a new direct coordinate angle.
scalarDirectionInference.usefulness: This prevents mislabelling the D defect as predominantly angular. It helps choose a coupled state representation, not an online gain knob.
scalarDirectionInference.limits: The best scale uses the native target. It repairs only the explanatory D component under its own denominator; it does not repair B, endpoint direction, finite admission, gamma response, padding capacity or the full consumer. No such correction was applied.
